summary: Confirmed DONE. All four parts of the proposal are on main. (1) Export is gated: AuthenticatedTracingBootstrap configures the OTLP exporter only when the primary server advertises observability.browserTracesEnabled (set when otlpTracesUrl is configured or RYCO_BROWSER_TRACES=1) or the build is a VITE_RYCO_PERF_PROFILE build. Otherwise it calls disableClientTracing and spans stay plain NativeSpans. (2) The default export interval is 10 s, matching the server. (3) The server's decode-failure warning logs only the cause and a span count, never bodyJson. (4) OTLP, FetchHttpClient and the serializer moved into clientTracingExporter.ts, which is dynamically imported. Two guards keep them out of the boot graph: a source-level test, and a bundle-budget rule on node_modules/effect/dist/observability/Otlp*. The changes landed in #710 (60633eff3: lazy exporter, 10 s interval, log fix) and 65af92766 (server-advertised gating). Both are in the Hub's vendored pin 7bc39eec3. I searched for missed paths and found none. Mobile uses client-runtime's noop tracer. Hosted-hub, hosted-static and hosted-cached sessions never mount the bootstrap. No other web or client-runtime module imports Otlp*. The server config atom is only cleared on hosted paths, so exportTraces does not flicker during local reconnects. The only leftovers are a few minor latent nits, none of which affect perf.

evidence.note: AuthenticatedTracingBootstrap computes exportTraces from shouldExportClientTraces and calls configureClientTracing() or disableClientTracing() in an effect keyed on exportTraces. It is mounted only when authGateState.status === 'authenticated' (localTracingAllowed).
Returns perfProfile || observability?.browserTracesEnabled === true. Older servers omit the field, so their clients export nothing.
isWebPerfProfileEnabled is a build-time constant from VITE_RYCO_PERF_PROFILE, not a runtime toggle.

browserTracesEnabled = config.otlpTracesUrl !== undefined || config.browserTracesEnabled === true. The env var is defined at apps/server/src/cli.ts:323 and the schema at packages/contracts/src/server.ts:338.

await import('./clientTracingExporter'). The exporter module (clientTracingExporter.ts:1-3) holds FetchHttpClient and OtlpExporter/OtlpSerialization/OtlpTracer. clientTracing.ts only imports its type.
Asserts that clientTracingExporter.ts is not statically reachable from main.tsx.
The bundle-budget rule forbids node_modules/effect/dist/observability/Otlp* in the boot chunks of the real dist.

DecodeOtlpTraceRecordsError now carries spanCount, not bodyJson. The warning logs { cause, spanCount } under the comment 'Never log the payload'. The old code (f1be4abc7 http.ts:291-297) logged bodyJson.
The default ObservabilityService tracingLayer is a noop tracer, so mobile and other clients have no OTLP export path.

clearServerState (which sets the config to null) is called only from hostedHub/environment.ts. Local authenticated sessions do not null the config on reconnect, so the gate does not toggle during reconnects.

Minor latent nit, not reachable in practice. configure() short-circuits whenever activeConfigKey !== null, even when a disableClientTracing() is still queued behind an in-flight apply. A true->false->true flip inside one exporter load would therefore end disabled. exportTraces only changes when the server's advertised config changes, so this does not happen today.

fixDefects: No real defects. Minor non-perf nits: (a) clientTracing.ts:65-68: the configure() fast path ignores a queued disable, so a rapid true->false->true flip during an in-flight exporter load would leave tracing disabled. This is unreachable today because the gate only changes when the server's advertised config changes. (b) clientTracing.ts:95-103: if the dynamic import or exporter start fails, activeConfigKey stays set and later configure() calls never retry. This was already true at f1be4abc7 and only affects diagnostics. (c) RYCO_BROWSER_TRACES is not listed in the docs/observability.md env-var section (around line 519). (d) Intentional behaviour change: the Settings > Diagnostics recent-spans table (DetailedTraceDiagnostics.tsx, source 'browser') no longer shows browser spans by default unless OTLP or RYCO_BROWSER_TRACES is set. The commit message documents this.
implementationSketch: Optional hardening only: (1) In apps/web/src/observability/clientTracing.ts, track a desired-state flag (desiredEnabled) that configure/disable set synchronously, and have the fast path in configureClientTracing return early only when desiredEnabled was already true and no disable is queued. Alternatively, clear activeConfigKey synchronously in disableClientTracing. Add a test that calls configure(); disable(); configure() without awaiting between calls and asserts that an exporter is active at the end. (2) In the catch branch of applyClientTracingConfig, reset activeConfigKey = null when generation === configurationGeneration so a later configure() can retry. (3) Add RYCO_BROWSER_TRACES to the OTLP env-var list in docs/observability.md. None of these change perf.
decisionReason: Nothing remains to decide. Making browser spans opt-in, which hides them from the default Diagnostics view, was a deliberate product choice already made in 65af92766.
